To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
prolonged expression of a transgene in animals can be achieved with adenovirus vectors even in the presence of an adenovirus-specific cellular immune response.
prolonged expression of hu AAT is achieved in mice that develop an Ad vector-specific cellular immune response.
Ad vector-infected cells expressing nonimmundogenic transgenes can escape adenoviral antigen-specific cellular immune killing in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of gene therapy vectors for use in the treatment of human disease.
the development of gene therapy vectors that are capable of prolonged expression of a transgene.
the development and application of gene therapy for the treatment of genetic diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prolonged expression of nonimmunogenic reporter proteins is possible in mice that are capable of mounting an effective cellular immune response to Ad vector-encoded proteins.
prolonged transgene expression is possible with Ad vectors in mice that are capable of mounting an immune response to Ad antigens but that the transgene must not elicit an immune response.
the Ad vector can direct long-term expression of a non-immunogenic transgene in the presence of a strong Ad-specific cellular immune reponse.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prolonged expression of nonimmunogenic genes is possible with Ad vectors, even in the presence of a cellular immune response.
Ad-specific cytotoxic T lymphocyte activity is not a major factor in the regulation of Ad vector-directed expression in vivo.
Ad vectors expressing a nonimmunogenetic transgene can be administered to mice that have been immunized with Ad vectors expressing a foreign transgene and can direct prolonged expression in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of Ad-specific cellular immunity does not preclude the possibility of long-term gene expression from an Ad vector in vivo, and that the presence of an Ad-specific cellular response may not be a limiting factor for gene therapy trials in humans.
Ad-specific cellular immune responses can be evoked by Ad vectors but that these responses are not effective against cells expressing non-immunogenic transgenes.
Ad vector-induced immune responses can be manipulated so that the immune response is directed against the Ad vector itself, leaving the transgene product alone to express.
